question: What has TfL said about publishing section-level noise data?
norm_question: what has tfl said about publishing section level noise data

answer.text: The retrieved documents contain no TfL policy statement on proactively publishing section-level noise data, though TfL published section-level cab noise data in FOI-2986-2324 and FOI-1231-2425 while turning down the majority of Elly Baker AM's data requests, citing constrained resources.

verified_claims.text: The retrieved documents do not contain a policy statement from TfL on proactively publishing section-level noise data, though they show what section-level data TfL has released under Freedom of Information requests and what Assembly Members and the Mayor have said about data sharing.

In FOI-2986-2324 (published 12 December 2023) a TfL case officer published a table of cab noise levels and 1/3rd octaves recorded on 4 September 2023 for the tunnel sections between White City and Newbury Park, and in FOI-1231-2425 (published 08 August 2024) a TfL case officer published section-by-section Central line cab dB LAeq readings recorded on 24 June 2024 and stated that readings are carried out on a bi-monthly period.

citations.quote:
Request ID: FOI-2986-2324
Date published: 12 December 2023

The attached table, which contains data taken on 4 September 2023, provides the levels and 1/3rd octaves in a Central line train cab recorded for the entire tunnel sections between White City and Newbury Park.

Request ID: FOI-1231-2425
Date published: 08 August 2024

Please see below the noise levels recorded on the Monday 24
June 2024, these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab.
Readings are carried out on a bi-monthly period.

verified_claims.text: According to Elly Baker AM's account at Mayor's Question Time on 16 July 2026 (Question 2026/2156), after she wrote to the TfL Commissioner asking for specific data based on residents' casework, she received an email from TfL's Government Relations turning down the majority of the requests for data and stating that while TfL is fully committed to tackling Tube noise, resources remain constrained.

citations.quote: I asked for specific data based on the residents' casework that we dealt with.

just an email from TfL's
Government Relations turning down the majority of the requests for data. It contained the reassuring phrase,
"We are fully committed to tackling Tube noise, but – as you have said – resources remain constrained".

verified_claims.text: At Mayor's Question Time on 16 July 2026 (Question 2026/2156), the Mayor of London stated that he would ensure TfL provides Assembly Members with far more detailed information, including real-time rail grinding activity over the next six months, track renewal programmes, alternative noise reduction measures, and a constituency-level breakdown of noise level complaints and action being taken.

citations.quote:
I will make sure it provides, in addition, information on what in real-time rail
grinding activity is taking place over the next six months, the track renewal programmes, alternative noise
reduction measures that are being considered or in delivery.

a constituency-level breakdown,
which is really important, of the noise level complaints and what action is being taken.
